#### 1. Schwartz-Jampel syndrome type 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.455)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-975634)

**Proposed mechanism:** PNLIP (HGNC:9009) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormality of connective tissue (HP:0003557); HSPG2 (HGNC:4879) —DISRUPTS→ Basement membrane assembly (GO:0007101); Basement membrane assembly (GO:0007101) —DISRUPTS→ Abnormality of collagen (HP:0003204); HSPG2 (HGNC:4879) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormality of collagen (HP:0003204); HSPG2 (HGNC:4879) —LEADS_TO→ Myopia (HP:0000545); Myopia (HP:0000545) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormality of the eye (HP:0000479). Mutations in PNLIP (associated with disease A) lead to connective tissue abnormalities. Mutations in HSPG2 (associated with Schwartz-Jampel syndrome type 1, disease B) disrupt basement membrane assembly, which in turn leads to abnormalities in collagen and ocular phenotypes like myopia.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the causal variants for MONDO:0013700 and MONDO:0100435 do not affect the respective genes (PNLIP and HSPG2) or that the downstream pathways are entirely independent and do not share any functional consequence. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared functional consequences of mutations in genes involved in extracellular matrix integrity could lead to the development of common therapeutic strategies targeting connective tissue health or basement membrane function for both diseases.

#### 2. maturity-onset diabetes of the young type 8  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.429)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-192456, Reactome:R-HSA-9925561)

**Proposed mechanism:** PNLIP (HGNC:9020) —DISRUPTS→ pancreatic exocrine function (HP:0001982); CEL (HGNC:2144) —DISRUPTS→ pancreatic exocrine function (HP:0001982); pancreatic exocrine function (HP:0001982) —LEADS_TO→ Pancreatic insufficiency (HP:0001982); pancreatic exocrine function (HP:0001982) —LEADS_TO→ Diabetes mellitus (HP:0005978). Loss-of-function mutations in PNLIP (causing Disease A) and CEL (causing Disease B) both disrupt the normal functioning of the exocrine pancreas. Impaired pancreatic exocrine function can lead to malabsorption and nutrient deficiencies, which may indirectly contribute to metabolic dysfunction and diabetes (Disease B), while also directly causing pancreatic insufficiency (Disease A).

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in PNLIP and CEL do not converge on shared downstream pathways related to nutrient digestion and absorption, or that the observed phenotypes arise from completely independent molecular mechanisms. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular underpinnings of pancreatic exocrine dysfunction in these diseases could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting nutrient absorption or metabolic compensation for patients with either condition. For example, optimizing nutritional support or exploring adjunct therapies for diabetes in patients with pancreatic insufficiency.

#### 3. familial apolipoprotein C-II deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.366)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-975634)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic PNLIP variant —DISRUPTS→ PNLIP (HGNC:9030); PNLIP (HGNC:9030) —DISRUPTS→ Triglyceride hydrolysis (REACT:R-HSA-184081); Triglyceride hydrolysis (REACT:R-HSA-184081) —DECREASES→ Free fatty acids (CHEBI:37735); Free fatty acids (CHEBI:37735) —LEADS_TO→ Dyslipidemia (HP:0003151); Pathogenic APOC2 variant —DISRUPTS→ APOC2 (HGNC:524); APOC2 (HGNC:524) —DISRUPTS→ Chylomicron and VLDL remnant clearance (REACT:R-HSA-184081); Chylomicron and VLDL remnant clearance (REACT:R-HSA-184081) —DECREASES→ Triglycerides (CHEBI:17581); Triglycerides (CHEBI:17581) —LEADS_TO→ Dyslipidemia (HP:0003151). Loss-of-function mutations in PNLIP (involved in triglyceride hydrolysis) in MONDO:0013700 lead to reduced free fatty acid production and dyslipidemia. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in APOC2 in familial apolipoprotein C-II deficiency impair chylomicron and VLDL remnant clearance, leading to elevated triglyceride levels and dyslipidemia. Both pathways converge on the phenotype of dyslipidemia.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of a pathogenic variant in PNLIP or APOC2 in individuals with MONDO:0013700 or familial apolipoprotein C-II deficiency, respectively, with a significantly different functional consequence (e.g., gain-of-function) would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, a lack of any dyslipidemia phenotype in individuals with these mutations would also be falsifying. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in gnomAD within the coding regions of PNLIP and APOC2 associated with MONDO:0013700 and familial apolipoprotein C-II deficiency, respectively, would challenge the causality of these specific genes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic link via dyslipidemia suggests potential therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism could be beneficial for both conditions. For instance, interventions aimed at improving triglyceride clearance or modulating fatty acid availability might offer a common therapeutic avenue.

**Why it matters:** Understanding this overlap could lead to novel therapeutic strategies for dyslipidemia by targeting shared pathways involved in triglyceride and cholesterol metabolism. For example, interventions aimed at improving HDL function might indirectly benefit patients with fat malabsorption, or vice versa.
